topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: From Bouncing Blocks to Digits of π

sections.title: The Setup: The Elastic Collision Paradox
lecture_lines: Two blocks move on a frictionless surface.
A small block approaches a stationary large block.
A wall sits behind the large block.
animations: Display two blocks [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg], small (left) and large (right), on a horizontal #FFFFFF line.
Small block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] moves right towards the large block.
Show a vertical #FFFFFF line [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg] behind the large block as a wall.

sections.title: The Pattern: Counting the Collisions
lecture_lines: Collisions occur between the blocks and wall.
The count depends on the mass ratio.
animations: Show small [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] colliding with large [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg], then large with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg].
Vary mass ratio between [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] instances visually by scaling the sizes.
Animate 31 collision cycles between [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] objects for a 100x mass ratio.

sections.title: The Bridge: Geometry in Motion
lecture_lines: Map block motion to circular geometry.
The angle relates to the mass ratio.
Collision count approximates the arc length.
Visualize the movement on a circle.
animations: Project [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] positions onto a unit circle as angles.
Show angle increment proportional to the square root of mass ratio.
Draw arc segments on the circle for each collision.
Highlight the mapping between physics and geometric arcs.
Display rotating vector to visualize motion around the circle using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].

sections.title: The Revelation: Calculating Pi
lecture_lines: Mass ratios reveal digits of pi.
Each digit emerges from the collisions.
animations: Show the mass ratio 100, 10000, 1000000 displaying digits 3, 1, 4 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].
Highlight the decimal digits appearing as collisions conclude against the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg].
Display the formula for collision count approximating pi.
Connect specific digit sequences to final block velocities using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].
Demonstrate the mechanical process of the block colliding with the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg] yielding digits of pi.
